sections.content: To ask “what?” about an object, use *mit*, the object form of *mi*. It takes the place of the food: *Mit eszel?* (What are you eating?) *Almát eszem.* (I eat an apple.) The answer repeats the verb, and the food takes *-t*.

sections.title: With meals
sections.content: You know *után* and *előtt* with the meals *reggeli*, *ebéd* and *vacsora*. They go well with these verbs: *Reggeli után kávét iszom.* (After breakfast I drink coffee.)
*Mi van?* asks what there is. *Mit eszel?* asks what you do something to, so it needs the *-t*. A reply usually leaves out the subject, as you know: *Almát eszem.*
